## Glyphling 0.9.3 (test build for 1.0)

Download `Glyphling-Setup-0.9.3.exe` below and run it. It updates an existing installation in place, keeping settings, themes and position.

### New
- **Volume target**: Settings > Music has a new "Volume app" row. It lists the apps that have an audio session in the Windows volume mixer (for example `spotify.exe`); pick one and the circle's volume lowers exactly that mixer entry. "Automatic" (default) follows the music app being listened to, matched by process name. If nothing matches, nothing is changed: the system volume and other apps are never touched.

- **Music app list**: the chip selector is replaced by a real list. Add the apps you want (from the ones playing right now, or with "Choose a program" to pick an .exe) and remove them with ×. The music mode shows and controls only those apps. An empty list means any app.

### Fixes
- **Title bar when unfocused**: the earlier fix could not take effect because the window was being patched from the wrong thread. All app windows are now patched on their own thread and become plain popups with no frame, caption or non-client painting.
- **2048 points lag**: the glow is drawn small and scaled up instead of blurring a full-size canvas every frame, and the circle repaints at 30 fps at that resolution.
- **Theme colors on the cover**: bright or flat covers no longer turn the whole circle white; brightness is now equalized over the cover so every cover uses the full range of the theme.

### Changed
- Removed the fallback that lowered whichever apps were playing when the music app's process was not found.
- Cover colors: ported the prototype's per-LED color path, so with the switch off real album covers keep their own colors.

The setup is not signed yet: Windows SmartScreen may warn on first launch ("More info" → "Run anyway").
